title: Combo Boxes and List Boxes
summary: Choosing one item from many is everywhere in tools - a material, a level, an enemy type. This lesson covers `BeginCombo` with `Selectable`, the simple `Combo` overloads, list boxes, filtering a long list as you type, and showing enums by name.
ideas:
- Make a material combo bound to an enum, with the name table and `static_assert`.
- Make a list of 200 generated asset names with a filter box above it, and select one.

cards.q: What does Selectable do and where is it used?
cards.a:
Draws a full-width clickable row that can show as selected; used in many list widgets

Selectable is the building block of combos, list boxes, tables and trees; you decide which row counts as selected.

cards.q: When would you use BeginCombo instead of the one-line Combo?
cards.a:
When items are not a simple string array, such as a vector of objects

The one-line Combo takes an array of strings or a "\0"-separated string; BeginCombo lets you draw anything inside, such as objects, items with extra drawing or a filtered list.

cards.q: What makes a good filter for a long list?
cards.a:
Case-insensitive matching where every word of the filter appears somewhere in the item, in any order

Then "rock big" finds "big_mossy_rock", which a prefix or exact-substring match would miss.

Only when BeginCombo returned true

BeginCombo returns true while the drop-down is open; calling EndCombo otherwise makes ImGui assert.

cards.q: Why add a static_assert next to an enum's name table?
cards.a:
So the build fails if an enum value is added without a matching name

The table and the enum must stay the same length, and the check costs nothing at run time.

cards.q: How do you size a list box to show eight items?
cards.a:
Use 8 * ImGui::GetTextLineHeightWithSpacing() as its height

The size is in pixels, and measuring in lines adapts to the font size.
